[[File:JohannesDroste.jpg|thumb|Droste (1908)]]
'''Johannes Droste''' (28 May 1886 – 16 September 1963){{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}} was a Dutch [[mathematician]] and [[theoretical physicist]], who was the second person after [[Karl Schwarzschild]] to solve [[Einstein's field equation]]. He was a professor of mathematics at [[Leiden University]] from 1930 to 1956.

== Biography ==
[[File:Johannes Droste. De huldiging van Professor Lorentz bij de Hollandse Maatschappij der Wetenschappen in 1925 (cropped).jpg|thumb|]]
On 27 May 1916,{{sfn|Rothman|2002|p=1541}} a student of [[Hendrik Lorentz]] at the University of Leiden,{{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}}  Droste presented his solution of Einstein's equation to the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.{{sfn|Rothman|2002|p=1541}} He obtained his doctorate in 1916.{{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}} From 1914 to 1919, Droste taught mathematics at the gymnasium in Gorinchem.{{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}} He then joined the University of Leiden and became professor of mathematics there in 1930.{{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}} Devoting himself to the teaching of mathematical analysis, he abandoned his research in physics, with the exception of a few contributions in elasticity and thermodynamics.{{sfn|Beenakker|2002|p=1543}}
